result.target_summary: Intel designs, markets, and services CPUs and other semiconductor solutions globally through its Intel Products business to consumers, enterprises, governments, and educational organizations, selling primarily to OEMs, ODMs, cloud service providers, and other manufacturers via various channels.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The current disclosure (2024) describes the general sales model, product design, and primary customer types (OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers). The search for a counterpart in 2023 did not identify a disclosure with the same specific subject matter. Candidate intc_2023_1A_D043 focuses on customer concentration risk (top 3 customers), while intc_2023_1A_D041 focuses on distributor/channel partner risks. Neither describes the general business-to-business sales structure and customer base definition in the same manner. Thus, no direct match found.

current_disclosures.summary: Intel designs, markets, and services CPUs and other semiconductor solutions globally through its Intel Products business to consumers, enterprises, governments, and educational organizations, selling primarily to OEMs, ODMs, cloud service providers, and other manufacturers via various channels.

materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure describes the general sales model and customer types (OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers). This is a standard description of the company's business model and market orientation. While introduced, it represents a clarification or reorganization of known business information rather than a new strategic shift or material change in customer dependencies.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Standard sales model and customer description

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: No counterpart found. The 2025 filing discusses risks related to the foundry business strategy (D003) and customer concentration (D035), but does not contain a general risk disclosure describing the scope of Intel's customer base and sales channels (OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers, resellers) as a primary risk factor in the same manner as the 2024 disclosure. The closest related risk is D034 (distribution risks) or D035 (customer concentration), but neither captures the general business model description of D048.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure provided a fundamental description of Intel's business model, customer base (OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers), and distribution channels. The removal of this overview in 2025, despite remaining specific risks (concentration, distribution), reduces the contextual clarity of the company's operational structure and market reach. This is a material change in the presentation of the company's core business operations and customer dependencies.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Removal of business model and customer base overview

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's dominance in the microprocessor market and its aggressive business practices, such as rebating, pricing actions, and exclusivity payments, may limit AMD's ability to compete effectively, potentially resulting in lower unit sales, lower average selling prices, and adversely affected margins and profitability.
comparisons.comparison: While Intel discloses its global distribution network to OEMs and cloud providers, AMD highlights that Intel's dominance in the microprocessor market and aggressive practices with those same top-tier OEMs create an uneven competitive landscape for AMD. Intel focuses on the breadth of its customer base and channels, whereas AMD focuses on the risk of being targeted by Intel's relationship-based market power.

sentences.text: We sell our products primarily to OEMs, ODMs, and cloud service providers.

Intel's microprocessor market share position, significant financial resources, introduction of competitive new products, and existing relationships with top-tier OEMs have enabled it to market and price its products aggressively, to target our customers and our channel partners with special incentives and to influence customers who do business with us.
These aggressive activities have in the past resulted in lower unit sales and a lower average selling price for many of our products and adversely affected our margins and profitability.

peer_results.rationale: AVGO candidates (avgo_2024_1A_D060, avgo_2024_1A_D065) discuss software cloud demand risks and product lifecycle management respectively. These topics do not substantively relate to Intel's Item 1A disclosure regarding its global distribution channels, customer base composition (OEMs/ODMs), and sales methods.

MU candidates (mu_2024_1A_D034, mu_2024_1A_D019) discuss system-level solution manufacturing costs and government support for competitors. Neither discloses details about global distribution channels or customer base composition comparable to Intel's focus on OEM/ODM/cloud provider sales structures.

NVDA candidates (nvda_2024_1A_D018, nvda_2024_1A_D016) discuss DGX Cloud service timing risks and general adaptation to industry changes. These do not address the specific topic of global distribution methods or customer base composition via OEMs/ODMs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Apple Vertical Integration History and Future
comparisons.peer_summary: Apple has used competitors' modem products and acquired Intel's modem assets in 2019, and expects to use its own modem products in future devices.
comparisons.comparison: Intel describes its role in selling to OEMs globally, implicitly relying on these OEM relationships for distribution. Qualcomm provides specific historical context regarding vertical integration risk within those OEM relationships, noting that Apple acquired Intel's modem assets to develop its own products, thereby changing the nature of the OEM-supplier dynamic Intel relies upon.

sentences.text: We sell our products primarily to OEMs, ODMs, and cloud service providers.
In December 2019, Apple acquired Intel's modem assets and is developing its own modem products using those assets.
Accordingly, we expect Apple to use its own modem products, rather than our products, in some or all of its future devices.
